- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid immediate overshoot.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates the peak in the middle of the horizon; cap forecast at 1–2% below the 14-day moving average of true outcomes.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.7, -0.4, +0.6), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
